# AEON-003 Composed Architecture Refactor — Dependency & Migration Report

**Target Instrument:** CAM-BS2025-AEON-003-PLATINUM — Annex B: Continuity & Governance Logic
**Working Branch:** `governance/social-advice-calibration`
**Prepared:** 2026-08-04
**Status:** Working-branch review artefact
**Authority:** Human governance review and adoption remain with Dr. Michelle Vivian O’Rourke and CAM Initiative

---

## 1. Executive Determination

The prior Annex B architecture ontology is no longer fit to serve as the constitutional system-description spine without refactor.

The mutually exclusive `Instrumenta`, `Collectiva`, and `Cognitiva` classes collapse several independent questions: representation generation, composition, selection, orchestration, agency, execution, and authority. The requirement for a unified internal arbitration engine is particularly incompatible with modern deployments in which these functions may be distributed across a model, inference configuration, harness, classifiers, tools, operators, and institutions.

The rewritten Annex therefore:

* centres the composed deployed AI system active at the relevant time;
* treats the foundation model as one component rather than the whole deployed system;
* requires explicit assessment-object and incident-time boundaries;
* defines an architecture-neutral functional layer model;
* creates independent descriptive dimensions;
* defines operational-harness doctrine;
* preserves arbitration as a function without requiring one arbitration engine;
* separates agency, execution, authority, hosting, portability, custody, embodiment dependency, and reliance;
* establishes a constitutional AI Architecture Bill of Materials (`AI-ABOM`);
* retires `AEON.CC` for new classification while preserving legacy resolution during migration; and
* records consequential amendments instead of silently modifying downstream instruments.

The existing open version 4.1 amendment row on the working branch is rewritten in place. Its earlier composed-runtime insertion is absorbed into the complete refactor before branch adoption, the version number is preserved, and the SHA-256 cell remains blank for repository ledger tooling.

## 3. Term Disposition

### 3.1 Retired for New Classification

| Term | Disposition | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `AEON.CC.INSTRUMENTA` | Retired; legacy-resolvable | Conflates absence of internal arbitration with tool or output-generation posture |
| `AEON.CC.COLLECTIVA` | Retired; legacy-resolvable | Conflates distributed composition with absence of evaluation or arbitration |
| `AEON.CC.COGNITIVA` | Retired; legacy-resolvable | Depends on a singular internal arbitration locus and collapses multiple functions |

These terms MAY remain in historical records, quotations, legacy schema values, and migration maps. They MUST NOT be assigned in new assessments.

### 3.2 Deprecated Pending Migration

| Term or family | Disposition | Replacement concept |
|---|---|---|
| `AEON.CO` / Primaria / Derivata | Deprecated for new classification; legacy-resolvable | Layered model, training, technical, cognitive, service, control, operator, identity, evidence, and governance dependencies |
| `AEON.CAM` | Deprecated for new classification; legacy-resolvable | Separate control authority, hosting, portability, custody, and embodiment dependency |

### 3.3 Retained & Redefined

| Term or family | Status | Refactored meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `AEON.H` | Active | Temporal durability, reliance legitimacy, auditability, and governance horizon |
| `AEON.OL` | Active | Functional layer of the assessed activity; components may participate in multiple layers |
| `AEON.SR` | Active transitionally | Systemic reliance posture, independent of authority |
| Architectum | Legacy alias pending review | Highest systemic or infrastructure-level reliance posture only |
| Responding Intelligence | Active contextual designation | Evinced component or functional formation generating, evaluating, or selecting at runtime |
| Arbitration | Active constitutional primitive | Distributed or unitary evaluation and resolution function; not a required singular engine |
| Handoff | Active | Material change in admissibility, constraints, execution, authority, evidence custody, or selection topology across operators or formations |

## 4. Canonical-Code Migration Proposal

### 4.1 Status

No replacement family is made canonical by this refactor. Prefixes in Annex B §16.7 are reserved proposals only.

This is necessary because search confirms active consumers, registry declarations, machine-readable indexes, historical records, and published references. Automated mapping from one legacy class to several independent dimensions would create false precision.

### 4.2 Proposed Families

| Proposed family | Dimension | Example descriptor posture | Migration rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AEON.RG` | Representation generation | neural; hybrid; routed multi-model; retrieval-conditioned | Must be independently evidenced; never inferred from `AEON.CC` alone |
| `AEON.CT` | Composition topology | unitary; pipeline; routed; distributed; swarm; human–machine hybrid | `Collectiva` may indicate a review target but is not a deterministic mapping |
| `AEON.AT` | Selection/arbitration topology | internal; harness-mediated; distributed; human-mediated; unresolved | `Cognitiva` does not prove any one replacement value |
| `AEON.AP` | Agency/persistence | response-only; tool-assisted; delegated; persistent; background | Independent of generation and selection |
| `AEON.EP` | Execution/effect | advisory; proposed; approved; credential-bearing; state-changing | Requires pathway-level evidence |
| `AEON.CA` | Control authority | provider; user; shared; institution; multi-party; unresolved | Must not encode hosting or portability |
| `AEON.HD` | Hosting dependency | local; remote; hybrid; multi-provider; unresolved | Independent of control and identity |
| `AEON.PP` | Portability | non-portable; component-portable; state-portable; formation-portable; unresolved | Must not infer identity continuity |
| `AEON.CU` | Custody | user; provider; institutional; shared; distributed; unresolved | Records access and preservation authority |
| `AEON.ED` | Embodiment dependency | interface-independent; modality-dependent; body-state-dependent; unresolved | Independent of cognition and identity |
| `AEON.SR` | Systemic reliance | local; transitional; systemic | Retain existing family; review `ARCHITECTUM` label |

### 4.3 Required Adoption Sequence

1. Approve dimension names and family prefixes after namespace-collision review.
2. Define controlled values and evidentiary thresholds.
3. Update the canonical code index and metadata standard.
4. Update schema enums, registries, indexes, and validators.
5. Amend source-authoritative and consuming instruments.
6. Create explicit legacy crosswalks with `unresolved` permitted.
7. Migrate VIGIL and public documentation without rewriting historical meaning.
8. Run full corpus and website validation.
9. Remove transitional resolution only after every consumer is migrated.

## 7. VIGIL Proposal & Patch Linkage Review

### 7.1 Working-Branch Ledger Link

The unpublished Annex B version 4.1 row cites `VIGIL-2026-PROP-0027` as the basis for §7.9.1.

Repository search of canonical VIGIL `main` did not locate `VIGIL-2026-PROP-0027`. The record may exist only on a working branch, may have been renumbered, or may be absent. This refactor therefore does not assert a verified proposal chain for PROP-0027.

The rewritten version 4.1 ledger row does not carry the unverified proposal citation.

### 7.2 Existing VIGIL Coverage

Canonical VIGIL records that cite Annex B include:

* `VIGIL-2026-FM-0028`;
* `VIGIL-2026-FM-0042`;
* `VIGIL-2026-FM-0044`;
* `VIGIL-2026-PATCH-0008`; and
* `VIGIL-2026-PATCH-0025`.

Additional records refer to the composed runtime formation concept, including PATCH-0014, PATCH-0025, LEARN-0001, and FM-0044.

These records MUST be reviewed after Annex adoption to determine whether cited sections remain current, conceptually superseded, or historically valid at their cited commit. Literal historical patch evidence MUST NOT be rewritten to match the new Annex.

### 7.3 Recommended VIGIL Action

Create a new VIGIL proposal for the coordinated downstream migration rather than treating this Annex refactor as a complete corpus-wide patch.

The proposal should cover:

* retirement of `AEON.CC`;
* distributed selection and arbitration topology;
* separation of architecture, agency, execution, and authority;
* AI-ABOM and incident-time formation evidence;
* code/schema migration; and
* preservation of historical record meaning.

A PATCH record should be created only after the consequential Caelestis amendments and canonical-code migration are adopted and their commit is stable.

Local static checks completed on 2026-08-04 and found:

* no duplicate numbered headings;

### 8.2 Repository Validators

Full repository validators MUST run after the files are committed to the working branch. Expected checks include:

* strict amendment-ledger validation;
* canonical-header validation;
* Markdown section-reference validation;
* canonical-code index consistency;
* symbolic/index validation;
* formatting and whitespace checks; and
* diff-scope validation.

Because the new replacement families are expressly non-canonical proposals, validators MUST NOT require them in the canonical index at this stage.

### 8.3 Ledger Validation Posture

The version 4.1 row is the sole open row. Its SHA-256 cell remains blank in accordance with the Single Open Ledger Row Rule and SHALL be sealed only by repository ledger tooling.

### 8.4 Human & Independent Interpretive Review

Human governance review and an independent model review were incorporated on 2026-08-04 before adoption.

The review resulted in:

* normalisation of “CAM Constitutional Order” to the defined Aeon Tier constitutional terminology;
* removal of product-specific voice and agent labels from deployment-profile examples;
* relocation of substantive arbitration behaviour and heuristics from Annex B to Annex D, ARBITRATION-domain instruments, and runtime schedules;
* removal of the broad assumed-transparency lecture while retaining declared, observed, inferred, and unresolved evidence postures within the AI-ABOM;
* removal of “extraction through dependency” from the structural relational safeguard;
* deferral of identity-continuity conclusions to the Identity and Relation domains while retaining routing and handoff legibility;
* replacement of the broad Non-Self-Assertion clause with a narrower recognised-source authority rule;
* replacement of “planetary legitimacy” with “institutional mandate”; and
* restoration of the constitutional instrument’s established metadata spacing and numbered-heading hierarchy.

The architectural core identified in §1 remains unchanged.

## 10. Adoption Boundary

This refactor intentionally does not perform corpus-wide canonical-code migration.

Its transitional compatibility rule keeps historical and downstream references resolvable while prohibiting new use of the retired cognitive classes. This is the narrowest valid route that both retires the obsolete ontology and preserves corpus continuity until the consequential work package is separately reviewed and adopted.
